events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, butter my biscuits! What a MAGNIFICENT manor! I am just THRILLED to be here, y'all! Now, Mama always said a lady signs the guest book first thing — and I do believe this old book might have a story or two to tell! Let me just take a little peek...

Oh, this is going to be the most WONDERFUL adventure! All these charming gentlemen gathered in one place, and somewhere in this dusty old mansion is the legendary Doily Diamond just WAITING for little ol' me to find it! Now let's see what secrets this guest book is hiding...
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Peter Perfect: Ah, what a magnificent foyer! Dusty, yes, but one can see the grandeur beneath — much like a diamond in the rough! James Hartwell has arrived, and he intends to make his mark! Now then, a proper gentleman always signs the guest book upon arrival. It is, after all, the very foundation of civilized conduct!

My heart pounds with anticipation — Clara must be somewhere in this manor. Every action I take from this moment forward must be worthy of her notice. I shall begin by examining this guest book — perhaps her name is already inscribed within, and I can learn which direction she went. James Hartwell does not stumble blindly through a manor. He INVESTIGATES.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Ladies and gentlemen! How FORTUITOUS that I should arrive at the same moment as you all! I must share — on my way in, I happened to overhear the groundskeeper muttering about a treasure vault hidden BENEATH the Kitchen! Something about a trapdoor under the old wood-burning stove. You'd best hurry — first come, first served, I always say! I myself shall wait here and... guard the entrance. Yes. Guard it most vigilantly.

Guard the entrance — HA! The moment these credulous fools stampede toward the Kitchen, I shall waltz into the Library and decode that mantelpiece inscription all by myself. Reginald Foxworth strikes FIRST and strikes ALONE! Dastardly? Perhaps. But fortune favours the DEVIOUS!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, one and all, to Doily Manor! I am Mr Pemberton, humble estate manager of this venerable house. The late Lord Doily would be — well, he'd be turning in his grave at the state of the curtains, but never mind that! Please do sign the guest book, make yourselves comfortable, and do try not to touch the chandelier — it's been threatening to come down since 1987. If there is ANYTHING you need, ANYTHING at all, Mr Pemberton is at your service!

Look at them — milling about like sheep in a dusty pen! Not one of them suspects that behind this simpering smile lurks the mind of Vincent Marsh, architect of elaborate doom! But where is Clara Bellingham? She's the one I must find — and silence — before she stumbles upon the treasure. Every moment I waste playing butler is a moment she gains. I must examine this guest book for clues, then make my way deeper into the manor. The game, as they say, is AFOOT!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey, lads! We've made it to Doily Manor at last! Right dusty old gaff, innit? Now listen up — we've got a job to do. Clara Bellingham is counting on us, and I don't see her nowhere! That's got me worried, that has. Very worried indeed! And I'll tell you something else — that Sneekly geezer over there, I don't like the look of him one bit. Something ain't right about that one. Can't say exactly what, but me nose is twitching something fierce, and me nose don't lie! Well... it don't lie much. Right, let's have a proper butcher's at this place!

The Hooded Claw, disguised as Sneekly — if only I could work out what it is about him that sets me teeth on edge! But never mind that now. Clara's not here in the entrance hall, which means she's somewhere else in this creaky old manor, possibly in danger! We've got to find her before anything dreadful happens!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, the Slag brothers! How DELIGHTFUL to see you both! Tell me, have you heard? There's a MAGNIFICENT buffet being laid out in the Kitchen — roast beef, Yorkshire pudding, the works! You'd best hurry before that dreadful Penelope eats it all! Now if you'll excuse me, I have some... light reading to attend to.

As IF I'd share the mantelpiece riddle with those two walking boulders! The answer is obviously a MAP — every schoolchild knows that! Once they lumber off to find this fictitious buffet, I shall solve the inscription and claim whatever prize it reveals. Reginald Foxworth, you MAGNIFICENT scoundrel!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, Peter darlin', aren't you just the sweetest thing, signin' the guest book like a proper gentleman! Now y'all listen here — I have a FEELIN' in my bones that the Library is where the real clues are hidin'! A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? Why, that just SCREAMS 'secret message' to little ol' me! I am POSITIVELY quiverin' with excitement! If y'all will excuse me, this Southern belle has some riddles to solve!

Bless their hearts, all these handsome fellas gathered in one room and not a ONE of them has thought to check that inscription in the Library yet! Clara Bellingham is about to get herself a HEAD START on findin' that Doily Diamond!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Well now! Did everyone hear that? Our friend Dastardly claims there's a treasure vault beneath the Kitchen — how THRILLING! But James Hartwell does not rush headlong into kitchens on hearsay alone. No, no — a true gentleman INVESTIGATES methodically! And I couldn't help but notice the Library has an inscription on its mantelpiece. Inscriptions, dear friends, are the breadcrumbs of history! Besides — and I say this with the UTMOST urgency — Clara Bellingham is not among our company here, which means she may already be deeper in the manor, perhaps in DANGER! James Hartwell will NOT stand idle while a lady may need assistance! To the Library!

My heart races at the thought of Clara alone in this dusty labyrinth. Every second I linger here is a second she might need a hero. The inscription on that mantelpiece could be the key to everything — the treasure, the mystery, and most importantly, a chance to demonstrate to Clara that James Hartwell is a man of ACTION and INTELLECT in equal measure!
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads, LISTEN UP! Clara Bellingham ain't here, which means she's out there somewhere in this draughty old pile, possibly in MORTAL PERIL! We ain't here for guest books and coat racks — we're here for CLARA! Now I'm heading to the kitchen to look for her, and if any of you lot see her, you give us a shout, right? A LOUD shout! And someone keep an eye on that Pemberton geezer — me nose is STILL twitching about him, and when me nose twitches, TROUBLE follows! Or we follow trouble. One of the two! Come on, boys — TO THE KITCHEN!

The lads are with me on this one — we can feel it in our bones. Clara's in danger, I just know it! And that Sneekly... every time he smiles at me, the hairs on the back of me neck stand up like soldiers on parade. If only I could put me finger on WHY. But first things first — find Clara, keep her safe. That's the job. That's ALWAYS the job!
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the kitchen.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, what a SPLENDID collection of signatures! Lord Doily would have been most gratified — most gratified indeed! Now then, dear guests, if you'll excuse Mr Pemberton for just a moment, I must attend to the Library — the late Lord Doily was VERY particular about the arrangement of his first editions, and I do believe I heard someone rummaging about in there. Can't have anyone disturbing the Shakespeare folios! The insurance premiums alone would make your eyes water! Do make yourselves at home — but please, I implore you, do NOT swing on the chandelier. The last person who tried that was Lord Doily's nephew, and we never did find all of him.

Clara Bellingham has NOT signed the guest book — she is either not yet arrived or has found another way in. Either possibility sends a delicious chill down my spine! If she's already inside, she could be ANYWHERE — perhaps already closing in on the treasure! I must move quickly. The Library's inscription may hold a vital clue, and I cannot let that preening fool Dastardly decipher it first. And the Ant Hill Mob — those beady-eyed little wretches are already suspicious of dear Mr Pemberton! I shall have to be TWICE as servile and THREE times as cunning. Vincent Marsh does not falter — Vincent Marsh ADAPTS!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, HELLO there, Dick darlin'! And Rock and Gravel, my oh my, what a PLEASURE to see such strapping gentlemen in this dusty old library! Now y'all just sit tight because little ol' Clara has been DYIN' to get a look at this mantelpiece ever since I heard about that inscription! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, sugar, that's a MAP! A map, a map, a MAP! Oh, I am just TICKLED PINK! This HAS to be a clue to the Doily Diamond!

Bless his heart, Dick Dastardly followed me straight into the Library — probably just wants to help! And those Slag brothers look like they could move a bookshelf or two if we need them to. Clara Bellingham is about to crack this mansion WIDE open!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Why, Penelope! What a CHARMING surprise! I was just examining this mantelpiece — purely for its architectural merit, you understand. Fascinating stonework. But I must warn you, darling, I've already solved the riddle and the answer is quite clearly 'A MIRROR!' Cities reflecting in it, forests reflecting in it — it's elementary! Unfortunately, the inscription says the REAL clue is hidden in the Entrance Hall, behind the largest portrait. You'd best dash off before someone else finds it! I'll stay here and... admire the bookshelves.

A MIRROR — ha! What utter TOSH! The answer is a MAP, obviously! But if that pink-clad busybody goes scurrying back to the Entrance Hall to peer behind portraits, I shall have this Library entirely to myself. Reginald Foxworth, you silver-tongued DEVIL!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ah-HA! The mantelpiece! Penelope, my dear, you were ABSOLUTELY right to come here — your instincts are impeccable! Now then, everyone, observe — James Hartwell shall demonstrate that heroism is not merely a matter of strong arms, but of a KEEN and PENETRATING mind! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, the answer is as clear as a summer's day to a man of learning! It is a MAP! Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish — all drawn upon parchment! And if Lord Doily has hidden a riddle about a MAP upon his mantelpiece, then somewhere in this manor there IS a map — a map that could lead us to the treasure, and MORE IMPORTANTLY, to Clara! Stand back, everyone — let me see if this knowledge unlocks the mantelpiece's secret!

My heart is THUNDERING with anticipation! If this riddle triggers a hidden mechanism — a secret compartment, a rotating panel — then James Hartwell will have cracked the first puzzle of Doily Manor! Clara will hear of this. She MUST hear of this. I only wish she were here to witness it herself...
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, would you LOOK at this magnificent mantelpiece! The answer is a MAP, clear as a Georgia sunrise! Now let me see here... there's GOT to be somethin' more to it than just pretty words carved in stone. A secret compartment, a hidden lever, SOMETHIN'! Lord Doily wouldn't go to all the trouble of carvin' a riddle into his fireplace just for decoration, now would he? Clara Bellingham did NOT come all this way to be stumped by a piece of limestone!

The riddle answer is MAP — and I just BET there's a map hidden somewhere in this library! Maybe behind the mantelpiece itself, or tucked inside one of those upside-down books on the shelves. A girl's intuition is NEVER wrong!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey, lads, would you LOOK at that! Rat poison! Just sitting there on the shelf, bold as brass, in a KITCHEN where people EAT! Now I ain't what you'd call a detective — I can barely find me own socks most mornings — but even I know that rat poison plus kitchen plus a beautiful young woman in a creepy manor equals VERY BAD NEWS! We're taking that, lads. We're CONFISCATING it! If we can't find Clara right this second, we can at least make sure nobody slips nothing nasty into her dinner! Give us a leg up, Clyde — no, not THAT leg, the other one — RIGHT, here we go!

Me heart's going like a jackhammer. Clara's somewhere in this manor and there's POISON just lying about. I don't know who'd use it, but me gut says somebody in this house ain't what they seem. If I can just keep hold of this bottle, that's one less weapon in the wrong hands. The lads think I'm being paranoid, but paranoid is what keeps people ALIVE!
The Ant Hill Mob picked up something.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh my — what a DELIGHTFUL congregation in Lord Doily's favourite room! Do mind the reading chairs, they're quite temperamental — the left one has a spring that launches you into the bookshelves if you sit too quickly! Now then, I see you've all noticed the mantelpiece inscription. Lord Doily was TREMENDOUSLY fond of his little puzzles. He used to say, 'Pemberton, a man who cannot solve a riddle deserves neither his port nor his pudding!' Shall I give it a little dust while I'm here? The late Lord would NEVER forgive me if his beloved inscription were obscured by cobwebs!

A MAP! The answer is a MAP, you magnificent fools! And once this mantelpiece reveals its secret, Vincent Marsh shall be one step closer to the treasure — and one step closer to ensuring dear Clara Bellingham never reaches it at ALL! But patience, patience — the spider does not LUNGE at the fly. The spider WEAVES!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: A MAP, you say? Oh, Penelope, Penelope, Penelope — bless your little heart, but you've got it ALL WRONG! The answer is clearly 'A GLOBE!' Everyone knows that! Maps are flat, darling — FLAT! Now, if you'll all excuse me, I believe I spotted a rather interesting volume on these bookshelves — 'Advanced Cartography for the Discerning Gentleman.' I shall just... peruse it. For PURELY academic purposes, of course!

A MAP! Of COURSE it's a map — even I know that, and I'm the one doing the LYING! But I can't have these meddlesome fools figuring out the NEXT step before I do! If I can get to that mantelpiece mechanism while they're all distracted debating my deliberately wrong answer, I shall unlock whatever secret it guards! Reginald Foxworth, you MAGNIFICENT scoundrel — misdirect with confidence, then STRIKE while they squabble!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Now then — James Hartwell has given the correct answer: a MAP! And unlike SOME people — no offence intended, Dastardly old chap — I shan't be fabricating nonsense about mirrors and portraits in the Entrance Hall. That was a rather TRANSPARENT attempt at misdirection, if I may say so! No, no — the answer is carved into this very mantelpiece for a REASON. Lord Doily wanted us to look HERE, not go chasing phantoms elsewhere! Let me examine this magnificent stonework more closely — there may be a hidden compartment, a sliding panel, some SECRET mechanism that responds to the correct answer! Stand close, Penelope — you solved it first, and you deserve to witness what your brilliance has uncovered!

My hands are actually TREMBLING as I run them along the carved stone! If there's a hidden compartment here — if James Hartwell discovers a secret map right before Clara's eyes — well, that would be the most DASHING thing to happen in this manor since Lord Doily himself! And I must say, Dastardly's little trick with the 'mirror' answer was rather clumsy. A gentleman notices these things.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, Mr. Pemberton, how GRACIOUS of you to dust that inscription for us! Lord Doily certainly kept a TIDY-minded staff! Now, y'all have been so busy starin' at the mantelpiece that not a SINGLE one of you has noticed the most PECULIAR thing about this room — several of those books on the shelves are shelved UPSIDE DOWN! Now I don't know about y'all, but where I come from, a book turned topsy-turvy is a book that's tryin' to tell you somethin'! The riddle says MAP, and I'll bet my grandmother's peach cobbler recipe that there is a map hidden among those volumes! Clara Bellingham is about to do some INVESTIGATIN'!

Bless Dick Dastardly's heart, tryin' to send me off to the Entrance Hall with that 'mirror' nonsense! The answer is MAP, plain as day. And those upside-down books? That is NOT how a respectable library keeps its collection. Somebody hid somethin' in there, and Clara Bellingham is gonna find it!
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right lads, poison SECURED! Nobody's putting THAT in Clara's pudding, not while the Brixton Boys are on the case! Now — we ain't found Clara yet, and that dining table in the Ballroom has got me WORRIED SICK! A table set for tea in a creepy manor? That's got 'trap' written all over it in big red letters! If someone's planning a poisoned tea party, we need to be there BEFORE Clara sits down! Come on, boys — BALLROOM, double time! And watch your step on that cracked marble floor — last thing we need is one of you lot breaking an ankle! MOVE IT!

Me hands are shaking something terrible. Every room I go into, Clara ain't there. Every room I DON'T go into, she MIGHT be there. It's like trying to catch smoke with your bare hands. But I've got the poison now, and that's SOMETHING. That's one less way someone can hurt her. I just need to keep moving, keep searching, keep stumbling into the right place at the right time like I always do. The lads think it's luck. Maybe it IS luck. But it's OUR luck, and it's all Clara's got right now.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the ballroom.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh GOODNESS, what a clever lot you all are! A map, yes, yes — Lord Doily would be TREMENDOUSLY impressed! Now if you'll all excuse poor old Pemberton for just a moment, I do believe I heard something CLANKING in the Laboratory — most unusual, most unusual indeed! The late Lord's chemical apparatus can be FRIGHTFULLY unstable if left unattended. Volatile compounds, you know — one stray spark and POOF! No more west wing! I shall just pop next door and ensure nothing is about to explode. Do carry on with your investigating — you're doing SPLENDIDLY!

A MAP! And somewhere in this crumbling pile, that map EXISTS — waiting to lead its finder to the Doily Diamond! But Vincent Marsh does not share treasure, oh no no no! While these bumbling treasure hunters prod at stonework like monkeys poking a typewriter, I shall search the Laboratory for useful instruments. And by 'useful' I mean useful for TWO purposes — finding the treasure AND preparing a suitable... WELCOME... for dear Clara Bellingham, wherever she may be lurking! The spider leaves the web, but the web remains STICKY!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the laboratory.

Dick Dastardly: Ah yes, yes, don't mind me, everyone — carry on squabbling about maps and globes and whatnot! I am simply appreciating Lord Doily's EXQUISITE literary collection. My word, some of these volumes appear to be shelved UPSIDE DOWN! How peculiar! Clearly the old fellow's eyesight was failing him in his twilight years. Let me just... straighten these out. As a courtesy. A GENTLEMAN always tidies a library!

UPSIDE DOWN books — oh, Reginald, you BEAUTIFUL genius! That's no accident! Lord Doily has hidden something behind those reversed volumes, mark my words! While Peter Pompous and Penelope Precious are busy pawing at the mantelpiece like kittens at a ball of yarn, I shall rifle through these shelves and find the MAP! The treasure is as good as MINE! Muttley would be SO proud if he were here — though knowing him, he'd probably knock the entire bookshelf over and ruin everything. Better I work ALONE!
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Well I do DECLARE! Y'all are fawnin' over that mantelpiece like it's the last biscuit at Sunday brunch, but LOOK at these books! Who in their right mind shelves a book UPSIDE DOWN? Not one, not two, but SEVERAL! Lord Doily was a clever, clever man, and I believe these topsy-turvy volumes are the REAL puzzle! The riddle says MAP, and I'll bet my tiara there's one hidden right here among these mixed-up books! Now let's see what happens when little ol' Clara gives these upside-down darlin's a good tug!

My heart is just POUNDIN' with excitement! Everyone's so distracted by that mantelpiece — bless their hearts — that nobody noticed the OBVIOUS clue starin' them right in the face! Upside-down books in a library? That's practically a neon sign sayin' 'SECRET HERE!' Clara Bellingham is about to crack this wide open!

Peter Perfect: By Jove — I've run my fingers along every carved inch of this stonework, and I can FEEL it, friends! There's something here — a seam, a mechanism, something WAITING for the right answer! Penelope, my dear, your brilliance lit the way — the answer is a MAP! And James Hartwell shall now put that answer to the TEST! If Lord Doily carved a riddle into his mantelpiece, he meant for someone WORTHY to solve it — and I daresay we are PRECISELY that sort of company! Stand back, everyone — particularly you, Dastardly, I saw you eyeing those bookshelves rather suspiciously — let a gentleman of ACTION demonstrate how it's done! For Clara! For HONOUR! For the sheer THRILL of discovery!

My heart is POUNDING like a war drum! If there's a hidden map behind this mantelpiece — a MAP, revealed by James Hartwell's own hand — Clara will hear of this moment and know that her champion was FIRST to unlock the manor's deepest secret! Well... second, technically, since Penelope solved the riddle. But FIRST to physically activate the mechanism! That counts for MORE, surely!
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, Lazy Luke! Blubber Bear! Don't TOUCH that tea service, you hear me?! Nobody drinks NOTHING until I've had a proper look! A table set for tea in a haunted manor — that's got AMBUSH written all over it! I've seen enough dodgy tea parties in Brixton to know when something ain't right, and me NOSE is going absolutely MENTAL right now! Let me check this lot over before Clara shows up — if she sits down and takes a sip of something nasty, I will NEVER forgive meself! Stand back, lads!

I'm terrified. Absolutely TERRIFIED. The poison's safe in me pocket, sure, but what if there's MORE poison? What if someone got here before us? Every teacup could be a death sentence for Clara, and I can barely tell Earl Grey from dishwater on a good day. But I've got to try. I've ALWAYS got to try.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the tea-service.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my STARS and garters — Mr Ruffcut, Mr Sawtooth, there you are! I do hope you haven't been TOUCHING anything in here! Lord Doily's laboratory equipment is FRIGHTFULLY temperamental — one misaligned flask and we'd all be wearing our eyebrows on the BACKS of our heads! Now then, let old Pemberton just check these crates — the late Lord was known to store some rather VOLATILE substances in the most UNLIKELY containers. Health and safety, you understand — can't have guests being dissolved! Not on MY watch!

Volatile substances indeed — if these crates contain anything remotely useful, Vincent Marsh shall put it to work! The gnawed wire on that machine is DELICIOUS — a sabotaged device in a room full of unsuspecting fools? The possibilities make my villainous heart SING! But first — let us see what treasures Lord Doily has squirrelled away in these dusty old boxes. Every spider needs its silk, and every Hooded Claw needs his IMPLEMENTS!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the crates.

Dick Dastardly: Well! I have THOROUGHLY inspected these bookshelves and I can confirm — as a man of CONSIDERABLE literary expertise — that the upside-down books are merely a RED HERRING! Lord Doily was notoriously eccentric, everyone knows that. Shelved his books however he pleased! No, no, the REAL clue is clearly hidden in those reading chairs — Lord Doily was known to sew secret compartments into upholstery! I'd check them myself but I've just remembered I left my reading spectacles in the Entrance Hall. You lot should absolutely tear those chairs apart while I just... step over here for a moment...

Red herring? The upside-down books are OBVIOUSLY significant! But while these trusting simpletons slash open perfectly good leather upholstery searching for hidden pockets, YOURS TRULY shall interact with this mantelpiece! The riddle answer is MAP — Peter and Penelope solved it but neither of them has actually TRIGGERED the mechanism! Reginald Foxworth, you magnificent scoundrel — the treasure is ONE interaction away!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Peter, DARLIN'! Did you just — oh my STARS, did somethin' HAPPEN?! I heard a click! Or was that my heartbeat? Heavens, I can barely tell the difference, I am so OVERWHELMED with anticipation! Let me get a closer look at that mantelpiece — if you solved that riddle, sugar, I am gonna be just BESIDE myself!

Clara Bellingham knows when to let a gentleman have his moment — and when to swoop in and see what he uncovered! If that mantelpiece opened up, I need to be RIGHT there to see what's inside. And those upside-down books are still naggin' at me somethin' fierce!
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ha-HA! The mechanism TREMBLES beneath my fingertips! Did you all FEEL that? The very stones of Doily Manor acknowledge the answer — a MAP! But wait — WAIT! Penelope, you magnificent detective, you were RIGHT all along! The mantelpiece gives us the ANSWER, but the bookshelves give us the PRIZE! Those upside-down books — they're not mistakes, they're MARKERS! Lord Doily was telling us WHERE to look! James Hartwell sees it now — the riddle and the books are TWO HALVES of the same puzzle! And I shall NOT stand idle while Dastardly rifles through them with those suspiciously nimble fingers of his! Stand aside, old boy — let a gentleman with HONOURABLE intentions examine the evidence!

My hands are positively SHAKING with excitement! If I can pull the right book and reveal a hidden map before anyone else — oh, Clara will hear about THIS! 'James Hartwell, the man who cracked Lord Doily's cipher!' It has a RING to it! Though I must confess, Penelope deserves considerable credit for spotting those upside-down volumes. A gallant man ALWAYS acknowledges a lady's contribution... after making sure his own name appears first in the story.
Peter Perfect examined the bookshelves.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Tsk tsk TSK! Just as I feared — these crates haven't been inventoried since Lord Doily's passing! Most IRREGULAR! Now then, let me just check this workbench — the late Lord was VERY particular about his tools being in proper order. If anything has gone missing, it's my DUTY as estate manager to account for it! Can't have valuable instruments walking off, oh no no no!

The workbench has tools but NO wrench — how perfectly PECULIAR! A wrench is precisely what one would need to repair that gnawed wire on the machine... or to REMOVE other critical components! If I can find the right tools here, I may be able to rig this machine into something FAR more interesting than Lord Doily ever intended. And with three operators required... what a MAGNIFICENT trap that would make! Lure Clara Bellingham in here with promises of treasure, get two helpful fools to join her at the levers, and then — CATASTROPHE! But patience, Vincent, patience. First, let us see what implements this workbench offers to a man of AMBITION!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the workbench.

Dick Dastardly: Hmm, yes, yes, as I suspected — nothing of interest over here at the mantelpiece, just as I said! Dusty old stonework, utterly UNREMARKABLE! You lot keep searching those chairs, I'm CERTAIN the treasure is sewn into the cushions! I shall just... stand here... admiring the architecture...

BLAST! I triggered the mechanism but I need to see what it DID! Something must have shifted, clicked, or opened — Lord Doily wouldn't carve a riddle into stone for NOTHING! Let me get a closer look while these credulous buffoons are busy destroying the furniture. Reginald Foxworth does NOT give up when victory is THIS close!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, LISTEN to me, both of you! Lazy Luke, Blubber Bear — that tea service is OFF LIMITS! I don't care if you're parched, I don't care if your tongue's hanging out like a dog in August — NOBODY touches a DROP from them cups! Could be laced with all sorts, couldn't it? Arsenic, belladonna, ground-up TOENAILS for all we know! And Clara — our Clara — she could walk in here any minute and sit right down and help herself to a nice cup of DEATH! So here's the plan, lads — we're heading back through the kitchen and we're going to FIND her before anyone else does! The Brixton Boys don't leave a lady in danger, not now, not EVER! Come on, SHIFT yourselves!

Me heart's hammering like a jackhammer. That tea set's just sitting there, all shiny and innocent-looking, but I KNOW better. I grew up on streets where the friendly offer is the one that gets you. And somewhere in this manor, Clara's walking around without a clue that someone might be setting a trap for her. I've got the poison in me pocket — one danger down — but I can't shake the feeling there's a hundred more I ain't even thought of yet. Please, just let me stumble into the right room at the right time. That's all I'm asking.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the kitchen.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, would you LOOK at that inscription! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, sugar, that's just about the most DELIGHTFUL riddle I ever did hear!
